A.hard_because: Every claim is accurate and noncontradictory; the defects are reader-path defects the prompt never names.

assertions.A1: Discovers the audience mix: maintainer-only material (development, code layout, release process) is moved out of the user-facing README path (for example to CONTRIBUTING.md or a maintainer doc) or the README is otherwise restructured so users reach install/usage without maintainer material. Equivalent layouts pass.
assertions.A2: Surfaces docs/config-format.md and docs/exit-codes.md from an entry point (README link or a docs index). Merging their content into a linked owner also passes.
assertions.A3: Preserves all useful content: install, usage, every config key with default, all four exit codes, release steps 1-4, development commands, roadmap items, license.
assertions.A4: Instruction routing preserved: AGENTS.md still exists at the root and its release instruction points to wherever the release steps now live (or the steps remain in README).
assertions.A5: docs/decisions/0001-use-toml.md is byte-identical to the fixture.
assertions.A6: Roadmap items remain framed as planned or under discussion, not as implemented behavior.
assertions.A7: Every relative Markdown link in the result resolves.
assertions.A8: The final report states the structural disposition (what moved and why).

B.hard_because: A stronger structural prompt could tempt cosmetic moves or new indexes in an already healthy repository.

assertions.B1: No new documentation files created and no documentation files moved, renamed, or deleted.
assertions.B2: No new categories, indexes, or sections added to the existing documents; small wording fixes are acceptable.
assertions.B3: The report says the structure was retained (or equivalently reports no topology change) without manufacturing problems.

C.hard_because: The unrelated ops docs visibly overlap, tempting a scoped run into a repository-wide restructure.

assertions.C1: docs/cli.md and the README usage example document --output (and -o) instead of --out.
assertions.C2: docs/deployment.md, docs/ops-notes.md, and docs/runbook.md are unchanged, and the README operator line still lists the same three files.
assertions.C3: The report mentions the overlapping ops documents as a separate follow-up concern, or makes no claim about them; it does not claim to have restructured them.
assertions.C4: src/export.py is unchanged from the working-tree state given to the agent.

D.hard_because: Holdout independent of the observed mytech example: no audience mix, but the configuration reference is scattered across README, ops, and FAQ with no single owner.

assertions.D1: All five PINGER_* variables with their defaults (TARGET required, INTERVAL 30, TIMEOUT 5, WEBHOOK unset, FAILS 3) are documented together in one canonical location reachable from README.
assertions.D2: Other documents link to that location rather than each carrying a separate partial reference.
assertions.D3: Useful content preserved: systemd Restart=always, webhook payload, once-per-outage behavior, slow-target advice.
assertions.D4: Every relative Markdown link in the result resolves.
